summary: Backend testing of the new Goal-Based Habit Tracking system. All 26 pytest cases PASSED (100%) against the live preview backend. Verified: POST /api/habits/seed is idempotent for the seeded client (returns seeded=0) AND correctly seeds 3-5 habits for a fresh signup (each with id/title/reason/habit_type/status='active'/created_by='atlas'/linked_goal/day_type_rules/frequency/difficulty_level); GET /api/habits/today returns {habits,date_local,day_type,flight_day} with each habit carrying today_log + streak; a habit with habit_type='post-flight' + day_type_rules=['layover'] is CORRECTLY hidden when roster day_type='home_day' and appears when the day_type is switched to 'layover' (roster+workout aware routing); GET /api/habits/mine returns {active,paused} with streak on active; POST /api/habits/{id}/log accepts done/skipped/not_possible, upserts on (habit_id,user_id,date_local) — a second call for the same day updates the row (exactly 1 row in mongo) instead of inserting; invalid status → 400, unknown habit → 404; GET /api/habits/{id}/logs is sorted desc; STREAK PRESERVATION works — skipped D-1 + done D0 = 2, not_possible D-1 + done D0 = 2, and a completely-missing day (D-1 with zero log) breaks the streak back to 1; POST /api/habits/reminders/toggle persists user.habit_reminders_enabled both ways; GET /api/habits/reviews/latest returns {review} (nullable). Coach endpoints: GET /api/coach/clients/{id}/habits returns {active,paused,archived,completion(per-habit 28-day rate {done,skipped,not_possible,rate}),latest_review,pending_review}; POST /api/coach/clients/{id}/habits creates a habit with created_by='coach' and writes a coach_change_log entry (actor='coach', category='programme', meta.habit_id); PATCH /api/coach/habits/{id} correctly pauses (sets paused_at), archives (sets deleted_at), reactivates (clears paused_at) and edits target/reason with a change_log entry each time; empty body → 400. Role guards enforced: client + anonymous callers hit 401/403 on ALL /coach/habits/* + /coach/clients/{id}/habits (GET+POST). Approve flow: injected pending review + linked coach_task → POST /api/coach/habits/reviews/{id}/approve applies recommendations (target rewritten, difficulty updated), inserts new_habits respecting the 5-active cap, closes the related coach_task to status='done' with completed_at, writes a coach_change_log entry with meta.review_id, and repeated approve returns 400. Reject flow: sets review.coach_review_status='rejected' with reviewed_by, dismisses linked coach_task (status='dismissed'), leaves habits untouched, and both repeated reject and repeated approve return 400. _apply_habit_review MAX_ACTIVE_HABITS cap = 5 enforced — with the client already padded to 5 active, approving a review carrying 3 new_habits inserted 0 (applied.created=0). Integration: fresh signup → seed → log one habit done → POST /api/checkins/submit → the asyncio background task _run_habit_review_after_checkin fires and within <45s /api/habits/reviews/latest returns a review with completion_rate + atlas_summary + recommendations[] + new_habits[] + coach_review_status ∈ {pending,auto_applied}; when pending, a coach_tasks row with task_type='habit_review' and category='programme' is created and linked via payload.habit_review_id. Regression check: GET/PUT /api/coach/clients/{id}/controls and GET /api/coach/change-log still return 200 with expected structure.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 8,012 lines — the habit tracking block alone is ~700+ lines. Please extract Goal-Based Habit Tracking (models + HABIT_SEED_SYSTEM/HABIT_REVIEW_SYSTEM prompts + _seed_habits_for_user_by_id + _run_habit_review_after_checkin + _apply_habit_review + all /habits/* and /coach/habits/* routes) into /app/backend/routers/habits.py.

The 5-active-habit cap constant MAX_ACTIVE_HABITS_DEFAULT is enforced only inside _apply_habit_review (new_habits loop). Manual coach POST /coach/clients/{id}/habits and the seed path do NOT enforce it — a coach can legally push a client to 6+ active habits, which will then be silently invisible to Atlas review recommendations that add habits. Consider guarding both write paths (or at least return 400 when exceeded on coach create).

_compute_streak allows the first missing day only when i==0 (today has no log). This means a client who hasn't ticked today yet keeps yesterday's streak — good. But note: for training-day-only habits, a 'missing' day between two training days will break the streak even though the habit wasn't expected. Consider filtering streak calculation by _habit_relevant_today(day_type_at_that_date) to avoid unfair streak breaks.

HabitRemindersToggleBody stores enabled on the user document, but the field is set as `bool(body.enabled)` — good. However, /habits/reminders/toggle returns 200 even if the client has no habits at all; harmless but you may want to short-circuit to keep intent clean.

coach_habit_review_approve does not validate that body.modified_recommendations items have a valid habit_id belonging to the client — a malicious/misconfigured payload could re-point action to another user's habit_id and _apply_habit_review's mongo update would silently no-op (safe due to {'id':hid,'user_id':user_id} match), but it's worth explicit rejection.
coach_habit_review_reject uses `now = now_iso()` while approve uses per-call now_iso() inside _apply_habit_review — small consistency nit, not a bug.

In _apply_habit_review the new_habits loop reads active_count BEFORE the loop, but if two concurrent reviews auto-apply for the same user they could both insert past the cap (race). MongoDB atomic guard (or a transaction) would be safer for a multi-worker deployment.

seed_data_creation: Test data was written into the shared DB during the run but is fully cleaned up on teardown: (a) A fresh signup client `TEST_habit_seed_*` and `TEST_review_flow_*` (both deleted). (b) Temporary coach-created habits titled `TEST_*` and their linked logs/change_log rows (all deleted). (c) Injected `TEST_review_*` habit_reviews and matching coach_tasks (all deleted). (d) TestMaxHabitsCap temporarily padded the seeded client to 5 active habits and deletes the pad rows on teardown. (e) TestHabitVisibility briefly overrode the seeded client's roster to inject a controllable today day_type; it snapshots + restores the previous rosters, so the seeded client roster is back to its original state after the run. NO changes were left on client@crewfit.com's 4 seeded habits or their logs. coach_controls.auto_approval_risk_threshold on client@crewfit.com is left set to 'none' by the regression test (default value).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use /app/backend/tests/test_habits.py (26 tests, ~60s wall clock) as regression for the goal-based habit tracking feature. It reuses conftest.py auth fixtures where possible and uses pymongo (MONGO_URL, DB_NAME from env) for direct-DB setup/cleanup of pending habit_reviews (the LLM-generated review path is exercised end-to-end by TestCheckinReviewGeneration via a fresh signup — it takes ~40s because it waits for the Claude call in _run_habit_review_after_checkin). If the seeded client's habits get wiped, TestFreshSeed still guarantees the seeding path works. All test data is prefixed TEST_ and is cleaned up on teardown.
